context.title: Teach Us to Pray
context.summary: Jesus teaches the Lord's Prayer and urges persistent asking. He answers the charge that he works by Beelzebub, offers only the sign of Jonah, and pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers at a dinner.
context.background: Luke's form of the Lord's Prayer is shorter than Matthew's and is given in answer to a disciple's request. Jesus' reference to the blood of Abel to Zacharias (v. 51) spans the first and last murders in the Hebrew Bible's traditional order, which ends with Chronicles.

customs.note: Families often slept together in one room with the door barred, so getting up meant waking everyone. Hospitality to a traveler was a serious duty.
A ritual hand-washing Pharisees practiced for religious purity, not hygiene.

watchFor: Ask, seek, knock: the Father gives 'the Holy Spirit' to those who ask (v. 13).
Six woes, three to Pharisees and three to lawyers (vv. 42–52).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Satan
people.summary: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

people.name: Jonah
people.summary: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries (2 Kings 14:25-27) of the kingdom.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Abel
people.summary: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain (Gen. 4:1-16). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God.

people.name: Zacharias
people.summary: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God (2 Chr. 24:20), which so stirred up their resentment against him that at the king’s commandment they stoned him with stones, and he died “in the court of the house of the Lord” (24:21).

places.name: Nineveh
places.summary: First mentioned in Gen. 10:11, which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described (Jonah 3:3; 4:11) as a great and populous city, the flourishing capital of the Assyrian empire (2 Kings 19:36; Isa. 37:37).

events.title: Blind and Dumb Demoniac and Following Discourse
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 12:22 – Luke 11:36. People: Jesus. Place: Capernaum.
